findings.finding: The company has beaten the top of its own revenue guide two quarters running: Q1 2026 $104.1m against $103-104m, Q2 2026 $108.2m against $106-108m. Q3 consensus of $112.77m sits below the $113m midpoint of the $112-114m guide, so repeating the pattern gives about $114m, roughly +1.1% against the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by 1.6% and the stock moved -2.41% after a 26% run-up into the print. Q1 2026 beat by 0.8%: +2.11%. Q3 2025 beat by 0.4%: +22.89%, a move driven by EBITDA guidance and a buyback rather than revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The pattern is public and consensus has not moved to the top of the guide ($112.77m against $114m). A beat at the top of the guide lands inside what the company has told the market to expect, so most of it is priced. Had the market priced a repeat, consensus would sit at or above $114m.
findings.independence: Q1 actual against guide from the Q1 8-K exhibit (source). Q2 actual against the $106-108m guide from the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/375299/grid-dynamics-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). The prior-quarter estimate-vs-actual table is on TradingView (https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:6445e19c7814a:0-gdyn-q3-26-earnings-eps-estimate-is-0-13-usd/).

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue range of $435-465m has not changed in three releases. With Q1 $104.1m, Q2 $108.2m and Q3 at about $113-114m, the $450m midpoint needs about $124m in Q4, +8-9% sequential. Q4 2025 grew only +1.9% sequentially ($104.2m to $106.2m). Consensus Q4 is about $119m (one source, August). A Q4 guide or narrowed FY range near $442-446m would land below both the $450m midpoint and the $119m Q4 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: the Q4 2025 revenue guide of $105-107m came in below estimates, yet the stock rose +22.89% on a stronger EBITDA outlook and a $50m buyback (https://www.webull.com/news/13777521222034432). Q2 2026: the FY range was reaffirmed and Q3 guided 0.9% above consensus: -2.41%. Revenue-guide misses have not reliably been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Management declined to talk about Q4 on the Q2 call ('I don't want to comment too much upon Q4') and attributed the high end to working days, billable headcount and acquisitions. Coverage reported the $450m midpoint as 'reconfirmed' and 'optimistic' rather than doing the Q4 arithmetic. A market that had priced a lower midpoint would not have bid the stock 32% in a quarter, above the $8.00-9.40 average targets.
findings.independence: The Q2 call summary records the refusal to guide Q4 and the factors behind the range (https://www.webull.com/news/15341695036892160). Q4 2025 seasonality is in the same March 2026 8-K (source), so that leg shares a document. The Q4 consensus has one stale source (https://tickflow.io/stock/GDYN/forecast).

findings.finding: The stock went into the print at a six-month high: $9.06-9.10 intraday on 10-29, +3.9% on the day, +15% on the month, +32% on the quarter, and up from $5.21 on Jun 25. That is above Finviz's $8.00 average target and near MarketBeat's $9.40, with Zacks cutting to Hold on Oct 15. The bar for the reaction is higher than for the reported numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the stock rose from $5.69 on Jul 24 to $7.06 on Jul 30 (+24%) into the print, beat, and fell -2.41%. Q3 2025: no comparable run-up, +22.89%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It is filed because it sets the bar for the reaction. If the run-up were already unwound, the stock would sit near its 50-day average of $7.90 rather than 15% above it.
findings.independence: Finviz performance and target data, 2026-10-29 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=GDYN). MarketBeat targets, 50-day SMA and the Zacks downgrade (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-grid-dynamics-gdyn-expected-to-post-earnings-on-thursday-2026-10-22/).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 non-GAAP EBITDA guide of $16.5-17.5m (about 15% margin) against $14.7m (13.6%) in Q2 and a $16.41m estimate at the time. Headcount fell from 4,964 to 4,838 in Q2, cuts management says were non-billable roles, which supports delivering or beating the margin step-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025's +22.89% was attributed to a stronger-than-expected EBITDA outlook. This name has paid for margin surprises more than for revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is public and lands inside it, so only an EBITDA beat above $17.5m or a higher Q4 margin guide is unpriced. Had that been priced, EBITDA consensus would sit above the top of the guide. The latest figure I found, $16.41m, sat below it.
findings.independence: StockStory has the Q3 EBITDA guide at $17m against $16.41m expected (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/gdyn/news/earnings-call/gdyn-q2-deep-dive-ai-acceleration-and-strategic-partnerships-shape-outlook). The headcount figures share the call document.

findings.finding: Peer read-through since GDYN last spoke is mixed. Infosys (reported about Oct 22-23) cut its FY27 cc guide to 1-2% citing AI deflation, with Hi-Tech -17.3% and Retail -7.7% cc. Cognizant (10-29 bmo) landed Q3 above the guide midpoint with Communications/Media/Tech +10.5%, but Products & Resources fell -0.9%, it trimmed the FY range to 4.0-4.4% cc and bookings fell -7% YoY. Accenture beat on 10-01 and GDYN rose +6.4% that day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct measure. GDYN moved +6.4% on Accenture's 10-01 beat ($7.88 to $8.38) and +3.9% intraday on Cognizant's 10-29 print, so it has traded with peer prints in this window.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy. GDYN's TMT growth (+36% YoY in Q2) comes from its own top two tech clients, not the sector. The stock rose through the Infosys print, so the market has treated the Indian weakness as not applying to GDYN.
findings.independence: Cognizant 8-K exhibit, 2026-10-29 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001058290/000105829026000039/exhibit9919302026.htm). Accenture, 2026-10-01 (https://finviz.com/news/397737/accenture-shares-rise-after-fourth-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-beat-estimates). The three peers point in different directions.

findings.finding: Of the $50m buyback authorised in Oct 2025, about $30.8m (4.4m shares) had been used by June 30, $17.3m of it in Q2. About $19m remains, cash is $298.4m and debt is negligible, so an upsized authorisation is a plausible capital-return item at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A $50m buyback announced with Q3 2025 results is cited as one driver of the +22.89%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference. No new authorisation has been announced, and the pace of repurchases leaves the program near exhaustion by year end.
findings.independence: The Q2 release balance sheet shows treasury stock rising from $2.0m to $30.8m (https://finviz.com/news/375299/grid-dynamics-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). That is the same underlying fact.

findings.finding: Client concentration is rising. The top customer was 17.4% of Q2 revenue against 15.1% a year earlier; top 5 were 43.5% against 37.5% and top 10 61.5%. The top five accounts are now all outside retail, and Retail (-0.7%) and Finance (-2.6%) shrank YoY while TMT grew 36%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance of a top-client ramp-down in the seven baseline prints. The Jul 2025 -16.44% followed a weak guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed, so it is a risk rather than news. It matters only if Q3 or the Q4 guide shows a top-account slowdown, and nothing found indicates one. Net of the rest of the company: the other ~57% of revenue (retail, finance, CPG) was flat to down, so growth depends on the top accounts.
findings.independence: Vertical split in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/375299/grid-dynamics-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Top-5 and top-10 shares in the call summary (https://www.webull.com/news/15341695036892160).
